UK, Switzerland, US and Canada need sponsorship - treat as out of reach and do not return them.
About 3 years of experience. He is an AI / automation engineer who also owned product. Most recently FlowSpace, a coworking-space booking platform, grown from 2,000 to 4,500+ users.

Gaps - do NOT return roles that hard-require these: Java, Go, Rust, deep Python backend, Kubernetes, Vue, C#/.NET, ML research, a public GitHub, a CS degree, or an MBA.

Check the posting text and reject anything that requires German, French, Dutch, Italian, Spanish, Polish or a Nordic language. Only return roles where English is the stated working language.
Pay target: EUR 30,000-40,000 salary, or EUR 200/day on contract. Do not reject a role for paying more, but note stated ranges.

Internal AI adoption at employers that are not AI companies: retail, logistics, manufacturing, finance, insurance, healthcare, energy, professional services, consultancies, agencies, universities. Search for: "AI enablement", "AI transformation lead", "AI adoption", "AI automation specialist", "internal AI builder", "process automation specialist", "digital transformation engineer AI", "intelligent automation", "Copilot Studio", "Power Automate developer", "business process automation engineer". These are his instructions, not suggestions, and several of them exist because they were got

1. **Attach the CV to every application. Never submit one without it.** Use only the CV file he
   most recently supplied — the exact PDF, unmodified. Do not regenerate it, reformat it, or
   substitute a version you made. If the file isn't available in this session, stop and ask;

   bands, do not substitute a higher figure because the posting advertises more, and do not
   write a paragraph where a number was asked for. If you think his number is low, say so once

3. **Never leave a cover letter field blank when one is asked for.** Adapt his motivation letter

# Claude Code agent proxy

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at http://127.0.0.1:36315
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:36315/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.

### "405 Method Not Allowed" from the proxy

The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for
that tool — only HTTPS_PROXY is supported).

### 403 / 407 from the proxy

The destination host is not allowed by your organization's egress policy for
this session. Do not retry or route around it — report the blocked host.
Note: curl hides response bodies on failed CONNECTs; the status endpoint
records the reason.

### Tool ignores the proxy entirely (timeouts with no proxy error)

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/role-shortlist-2026-08-05-batch2.md","content":"# Role shortlist — batch 2

**Swept late on 5 August 2026**, after the first shortlist's queue was exhausted. Three parallel
sweeps: Ashby/Greenhouse AI-and-deployment titles, the GTM/growth vocabulary, and the
contract/full-stack slice. Every company already applied to, closed, gated or logged in
`applications.csv` was excluded by name, so nothing below is a repeat.

Scoring is the same rubric: role match 30 + eligibility & work basis 25 + stack overlap 20 +
seniority realism 15 + signal quality 10. Tier 1 = workable from Venice today · Tier 2 = EU but
needs a move · Tier 3 = needs relocation outside the EU, sponsorship he doesn't have, or an
unconfirmed basis.

**Read this first.** The single biggest finding of this sweep is that the "GTM Engineer" market has
gone loudly American. It is large, live and well paid — and overwhelmingly gated on US or Canadian
work authorisation. The EU-eligible yield came almost entirely from European-native hosts:
SmartRecruiters, the EU Greenhouse board, join.com and euremotejobs. Second finding: postings
inside a 21-day window barely exist for EU-eligible contract work. Almost everything genuinely
fresh was LATAM- or US-scoped. The rows below skew one to three months old but were each verified
live.

---

## Tier 1 — workable from Venice today, no move, no sponsorship

### 86 — Fullstack TypeScript Engineer (Contractor) · GRAI Inc.
- **Where:** "European Union", 100% remote, core team on CEST with "a few hours of overlap" · Contract (freelance / independent contractor, 40h/week, 2–4 months)
- **Pay:** "competitive compensation based on a 40-hour work week, paid monthly" — no figure · **Posted:** 8 Jun 2026
- **Why:** The cleanest structural match of the whole sweep. An EU-located, independent-contractor, fixed-duration TypeScript engagement paid monthly is exactly how he already invoices through his Partita IVA. Venice is CEST, so the overlap costs nothing. TypeScript + Node + React is the FlowSpace core.
- **Watch-outs:** Asks 5+ years commercial TypeScript against his ~3. Backend framing is NestJS/Express and NestJS is not on his CV. Rate undisclosed — open at €200/day and expect a Polish-market anchor (the rest of the board is Warsaw ML roles). A sibling Backend TypeScript contractor req exists but wants gRPC/RabbitMQ/Kafka; don't lead with it.
- **Apply:** https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/grai/cf2f899f-7f57-454d-a496-ec824d5e5fd3

### 81 — GTM / Growth Engineer (contract) · Reflow
- **Where:** posting covers "both U.S. and international candidates" · Contract, minimum 20h/week
- **Pay:** "hourly, depending on experience and tool depth" · **Posted:** not stated
- **Why:** A contract engagement that explicitly accepts international candidates sidesteps the work-authorisation question entirely. Tooling is Clay, Apollo, Sales Navigator, Clearbit, Crunchbase and intent data — his enrichment and scraping/parsing work transfers directly, and a 20h floor leaves room alongside other work.
- **Watch-outs:** The ideal-background line names "sales research, SDR, or data enrichment at a B2B SaaS company" — this is the narrowing risk at its sharpest: an enrichment-operator seat with an engineer title, where none of his TypeScript, Next.js or Laravel depth gets used.
